methodological_rigor.justification: This single-center retrospective series of 29 consecutive PCNSL patients uses Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and log-rank testing to evaluate prognostic factors including pre-biopsy corticosteroid exposure, MRI-to-biopsy interval, and MSKCC classification. With only 29 patients and a median follow-up of 19.5 months, the study is severely underpowered: the pre-biopsy steroid OS association did not reach significance (p=0.127), MRI-to-biopsy interval showed only a trend (p=0.074), and multivariate Cox regression was not performed due to insufficient events. MSKCC validation (p=0.038) is the only nominally significant finding. No propensity adjustment, no control for heterogeneous treatment regimens, and 10-year study period introducing treatment heterogeneity further limit interpretability.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a retrospective single-center case series (LoE 4) addressing the clinically relevant questions of whether pre-biopsy steroid exposure and biopsy timing affect PCNSL outcomes. These are important practical questions—pre-biopsy steroids can compromise diagnostic yield and potentially affect outcomes. However, the extremely small sample size (n=29), absence of significant primary findings, and inability to perform multivariate analysis severely limit the clinical contribution. The study cannot reliably quantify the prognostic impact of steroids or biopsy timing beyond confirming previously established MSKCC prognostic stratification.

reporting_quality.justification: The study follows observational reporting conventions with explicit eligibility criteria, consecutive patient enrollment, and appropriate Kaplan-Meier methodology. Limitations including small sample size, single-center design, and inability to perform multivariate analysis are transparently acknowledged. Survival curves with log-rank p-values are provided. However, treatment heterogeneity across the 10-year period (2012-2022) is acknowledged but not systematically addressed. No public data repository is mentioned. The manuscript appropriately frames findings as exploratory and hypothesis-generating given the limitations.

novelty_literature.justification: The prognostic impact of pre-biopsy corticosteroids and biopsy timing in PCNSL has been investigated in prior larger series. The MSKCC score validation—the primary significant finding—is a well-established tool. This small Turkish single-center series does not substantially advance understanding beyond confirming MSKCC validity in a local population and generating hypothesis-level data on steroid exposure and biopsy timing. The limited geographic representation adds marginal context but does not constitute a meaningful advance over the existing literature.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is competently written and adequately organized, with clear presentation of patient characteristics, treatment protocols, and survival analyses. The discussion appropriately contextualizes findings within the PCNSL literature. Limitations are explicitly enumerated with appropriate statistical caveats. The manuscript could benefit from more rigorous discussion of the clinical implications of the non-significant steroid finding—specifically whether the effect size (despite non-significance) remains clinically meaningful and whether a prospectively powered study is warranted.

key_strengths: Consecutive patient enrollment from a defined 10-year period minimizes selection bias within the single-center design
Transparent reporting of statistical limitations including inability to perform multivariate analysis due to insufficient events
Addresses clinically relevant questions about pre-biopsy steroid impact and biopsy timing in PCNSL—practical issues faced by neurosurgeons and neurologists
MSKCC score validation in a Turkish academic center adds modest geographic generalizability data
key_concerns: Severely underpowered (n=29) with no significant primary findings for steroid exposure (p=0.127) or biopsy timing (p=0.074), limiting all conclusions to hypothesis-generating status
No multivariate Cox regression possible given insufficient events, preventing adjustment for critical confounders (age, performance status, treatment regimen)
10-year study period (2012-2022) encompasses significant evolution in PCNSL treatment protocols, introducing substantial treatment heterogeneity as a confounder
Limited novelty given prior larger series addressing the same clinical questions with more definitive results
chief_reviewer.rationale: This small exploratory case series provides no significant new prognostic findings for PCNSL beyond MSKCC score validation, and the severely underpowered design prevents reliable conclusions about pre-biopsy steroid exposure or biopsy timing; Tier 4 (lower-tier specialty journal) is the most appropriate venue, with minor revisions to reframe as hypothesis-generating and more explicitly quantify the clinical significance of the non-significant effect sizes.
